summary: Nalini Balbir is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Colette Caillat (~1977–1980). She held posts at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (Professor, ~1988–2023), EPHE (Directeur d'études, ~2000–2023), and INALCO (attested 1998).

Nalini Devdas is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. She earned her PhD from Concordia University under Leslie Orr (attested 2004) and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2004).

Nam-lin Hur is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at Princeton under Helen Hardacre. He later became a professor at the University of British Columbia.

Naman P. Ahuja works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London and held a post as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).
Namita Das is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University, where she was supervised by Sibnath Sarma (attested 2012).

Namkhai Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Derge Gonchen Monastery and other monastic shedras, he taught Tibetan at Southwest Minzu University (~1958–1960) and served as professor at the University of Naples Federico II (~1964–1992).

Nancy Grace Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed graduate work at Columbia University and earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, studying under teachers including Bryan J. Cuevas and Michael Hahn.

Nancy Hock is a historian, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her PhD at UC Berkeley in 1987 under Joanna Gottfried Williams. In 1987, she held an attested post at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco.

Nancy McCagney is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, and others. In 1997, she held an attested post at the University of Delaware.

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She has served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).

Nanigopal Majumdar was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist. He served as a Superintendent with the Archaeological Survey of India (1931) and later as Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum (attested 1939).

Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1980–1985), worked there as a research assistant and lecturer (~1985–1993), and later served as a professor at Koyasan University (~2000–2021).
Naoki Nabeshima is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2004).

Naoko Nishimura is an Indologist and linguist who completed her PhD at Tohoku University by 2002. Studying under Toshifumi Goto, she later worked as a specialized researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2012).

Naomi Appleton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner, holding posts at Cardiff University and the University of Edinburgh (attested 2015).

Naoshiro Tsuji was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Oxford. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960) and later directed the Toyo Bunko (~1974–1979).
Naoya Funahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held a post at Otani University (attested 1981) and worked as a research fellow for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.
Narada Mahathera was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ceylon University College (~1921) and was trained by the traditional teacher Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1916–1955).

Narayan Hemandas Samtani was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Delhi (1957–1961) and later served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1961–1984).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and religious studies who held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from roughly 1967 to 1999.
